_note: for when you have no knife: 2 stones and 3 hours of sharpening; offered once a knife is needed (the spear)

log: You grind one stone against the other, hour after hour, until an edge comes up that cuts.
Three hours of grinding stone on stone. The edge is rough, but it cuts.
You knock flakes off one stone with the other, then grind the edge. It will never be a knife, but it will do.
You hack the straightest branch to a point with the rock knife. It is slow, blunt work.
The rock knife chews more than it cuts, but at last the branch has a point.
Stroke after stroke with the stone blade, until the tip is sharp enough.

ways.requiresText: Needs a knife. Without one, grind two stones into a rock knife first
log: You choose the straightest branch and carve it to a point with the knife.
You pick the straightest branch and whittle the tip sharp.
Shaving by shaving, the knife turns a branch into a point.

_note: needs a knife: the real one 30 min; the rock knife takes twice as long (Item.substitutes)

log: You knock one stone against another until it has an edge, and lash it into a split branch.
Stone on stone until one has an edge. Then a split branch, and the stone wedged in tight.
A sharp stone, a stout branch, and a long time binding them.
You lash a flat stone across the end of a log handle.
A flat stone, a handle cut from a log, a lot of cord.
You bind a flat stone crosswise to a handle. A hoe, of sorts.
